name: London Boroughs
description: Greater London is the metropolitan county encompassing London and its 32 boroughs, with the City of London forming a separate ceremonial county. It is England's largest urban area and a global centre for finance, culture, government, education and the creative industries.

places.name: Kensington and Chelsea
places.description: London's smallest and one of its wealthiest boroughs, home to the Natural History Museum, Portobello Road Market, and the King's Road.

places.name: Ealing
places.description: A West London borough nicknamed 'Queen of the Suburbs' for its leafy Victorian and Edwardian streets, home to Ealing Studios, one of the world's oldest continuously working film studios.

places.name: Havering
places.description: An outer East London borough with a semi-rural character, including the historic market town of Romford and green belt countryside toward Essex.

places.name: Newham
places.description: An East London borough that hosted the 2012 Olympic Park, home to Stratford's regeneration, the Westfield shopping centre, and one of London's most ethnically diverse populations.

places.name: Barking and Dagenham
places.description: An East London borough with deep working-class roots in the Ford Dagenham car plant, once one of Europe's largest car factories.

places.name: Barnet
places.description: A large North London borough combining suburban character with the historic Barnet Fair and the site of a decisive 1471 Wars of the Roses battle.

places.name: Bexley
places.description: A southeast London borough on the edge of Kent, home to Danson House, an 18th-century Palladian villa, and a mostly suburban, green character.

places.name: Brent
places.description: A northwest London borough home to Wembley Stadium, the national home of English football, and one of the capital's most multicultural populations.

places.name: Bromley
places.description: A large, leafy South London borough, birthplace of Charles Darwin's theories developed at nearby Down House, and one of London's greenest boroughs.

places.name: Camden
places.description: An inner North London borough famous for Camden Market, its punk and music heritage, and the intellectual legacy of Bloomsbury's literary set nearby.

places.name: Croydon
places.description: A large South London borough that grew into a major commercial and transport hub, with striking 1960s-70s tower blocks alongside a historic core around Croydon Minster.

places.name: Enfield
places.description: A North London borough combining suburban streets with historic Forty Hall, a Jacobean mansion, and the site of a former royal armaments factory.

places.name: Greenwich
places.description: A southeast London borough home to the Royal Observatory and the Prime Meridian, the Cutty Sark, and a UNESCO World Heritage maritime quarter.

places.name: Hackney
places.description: An inner-city London borough that transformed from industrial East End grit into one of the capital's most creative, fashionable districts. Home to Broadway Market, Victoria Park, and a nightlife and street-art scene centred on Shoreditch's northern edge.

places.name: Hammersmith and Fulham
places.description: A West London borough combining riverside Fulham with Hammersmith's theatres and the Apollo, one of London's best-known live music venues.

places.name: Haringey
places.description: A North London borough combining the leafy streets of Muswell Hill with Tottenham's football heritage and diverse communities.

places.name: Harrow
places.description: A northwest London borough best known for Harrow School, one of England's most famous public schools, founded in 1572 and set on a hill above the town.

places.name: Hillingdon
places.description: A large West London borough home to Heathrow Airport and the historic market town of Uxbridge.

places.name: Hounslow
places.description: A West London borough home to Kew Gardens' neighbouring areas, Chiswick's riverside, and a large South Asian community around Southall.

places.name: Islington
places.description: An inner North London borough combining Georgian terraces with a lively restaurant and theatre scene along Upper Street.

places.name: Kingston upon Thames
places.description: A southwest London borough centred on a historic market town where several Anglo-Saxon kings were crowned, marked today by the Coronation Stone outside the Guildhall.

places.name: Lambeth
places.description: A South London borough stretching from the South Bank to Brixton, home to the London Eye, the Imperial War Museum, and one of the capital's most historic Caribbean communities centred on Brixton Market.

places.name: Lewisham
places.description: A South London borough with a lively market and strong Caribbean cultural heritage, alongside green space at Blackheath's southern edge.

places.name: Merton
places.description: A South London borough home to Wimbledon and the All England Lawn Tennis Club, host of the world's oldest tennis championship since 1877.

places.name: Redbridge
places.description: An outer East London borough combining suburban streets with Epping Forest's southern reaches and one of London's largest South Asian communities.

places.name: Richmond upon Thames
places.description: London's only borough spanning both banks of the Thames, home to Richmond Park, the capital's largest Royal Park, and Kew Gardens' botanical collections.

places.name: Southwark
places.description: A South London borough home to the Shard, Borough Market, and the Tate Modern, spanning some of the capital's most historic riverside districts.

places.name: Sutton
places.description: A South London borough on the capital's southern fringe, largely suburban with the historic Nonsuch Park among its green spaces.

places.name: Tower Hamlets
places.description: An East London borough spanning historic Whitechapel to the modern skyscrapers of Canary Wharf, one of London's most rapidly transformed areas.

places.name: Waltham Forest
places.description: A northeast London borough covering part of Epping Forest and the historic William Morris Gallery, honouring the designer who was born in the area.

places.name: Wandsworth
places.description: A South London borough stretching along the Thames, combining the green expanse of Wandsworth Common with riverside developments at Battersea.

places.name: Westminster
places.description: The London borough at the heart of British government and royalty, home to the Houses of Parliament, Buckingham Palace, and Westminster Abbey.
